function: Knowledge-guided TD3 deep reinforcement learning jointly designs the AirComp transceiver (receive beamforming, transmit powers, denoising factor) for over-the-air gradient aggregation in federated graph learning (p. 7).
system: Edge server with N antennas and K single-antenna devices, uplink block-fading channel, no RIS; carrier frequency not stated (p. 2, p. 4).
method: Reinforcement learning: TD3 actor-critic (fully connected layers) with Lyapunov decomposition and closed-form transmit power as prior knowledge; pre-trained offline, updated online (p. 7-9).
data_channel: Simulated Rayleigh fading with path loss d^-3.5, devices in a circle of radius 25; FL data from TUDataset graphs with a GIN model (p. 9).
test_conditions: DRL policy pre-trained 20000 rounds, tested on the same simulated Rayleigh channel model; sweeps over antennas N and devices K, with training time listed per K (p. 9, 11).
baselines: Optimization-based alternating algorithm (KKT conditions), DRL without prior knowledge (same TD3 without Lemma 4), and error-free upper bound; no cited earlier design (p. 9-10).
metrics: Training loss and test accuracy versus communication rounds, antennas and devices; time consumption (training, inference, sum) in seconds (p. 10-11).
complexity: Measured time (Table I): inference 4.9e-04 to 5.1e-04 s versus 0.137 to 0.193 s for optimization, at least 277 times faster; complexity linear in input dimension (p. 11-12).
openness: Code said to be uploaded to GitHub, but no URL is given; learning data are public TUDataset graphs; no channel data released (p. 9).
q1_support: p. 9: "We consider Rayleigh fading channels" with its own path loss d^-3.5 in a custom simulator; no 3GPP, DeepMIMO, or measured channel is used.
q2_support: p. 11: "We evaluate the test accuracy with respect to the number of antennas at the edge server" is only a sweep; the paper never says a policy trained for one N or K is tested on another, the action space changes with N, and Table I lists a training time per K, so each setting seems retrained.
q3_support: p. 9: "compared with an optimization-based algorithm, a DRL-based algorithm without knowledge, and an error-free scheme"; the optimization algorithm is the non-learned baseline, but the DRL without knowledge is the proposed TD3 without Lemma 4 (an ablation) and no earlier published aggregation design is compared.
q4_support: p. 11: "Table I presents the average time consumption under varying number of edge devices"; p. 11: "at least a 277 times improvement" in inference time over the optimization-based method (about 5e-04 s per inference).
q5_support: p. 9: "uploaded the code to GitHub" gives no URL or DOI (the PDF has no link there either); TUDataset is a public dataset of the learning task alone and the channel is simulated, so no public channel data is used.
notes: Included, area 7: the learned DRL policy designs the AirComp transceiver for over-the-air aggregation (p. 7). The server has N antennas (p. 2), so the single-antenna check does not apply. RIS appears only in related work (p. 2). q5 is borderline: a GitHub upload is claimed on p. 9 without any link, so it is marked 0 under the link-or-DOI requirement and the reviewer may set it to 1 if the repository is found.
